newsitem.title: UK: UK cereal drought concerns overdone, analysts say.
newsitem.headline: UK cereal drought concerns overdone, analysts say.

text.p: Fears that drought is hitting Britain's grains crop are overdone, according to farmers and farm sector analysts.
Traders' concerns that the developing crop is not getting enough moisture have helped bolster grains prices in recent days, while the rest of the population basked in sunny holiday weather.
But any effect is likely to be minimal, analysts said.
"Everyone last year was concerned about drought and then we had the biggest crop ever," one said.
He noted that grains last year responded to the shortage of moisture by putting down deep roots, which appeared only to assist their development. "It could be the best thing that happens," he said.
Root crops like sugar beet and potatoes were more likely to be affected than grains, he said.

A co-op manager in eastern England also felt the likely effect would be minimal. "It maybe just stressing some crops which are too thick anyway, or affecting crops on very light land," he said. "But it's a minute amount as a percentage of the crop. If we get half an inch of rain now everybody will be smiling."

A farming source in the same area highlighted concerns not over the actual amount of moisture in the ground for plants to take up, but over the likely effect of low rainfall on the amount of water farmers are allowed to extract for irrigation. "There's the possibility of controls later in the season," she said.
All analysts said it was too early to make any confident predictions on the crop, but all were optimistic. "It's racing ahead," one said. "The crop is fairly motoring," another said.
Farmers had got their spraying done and their fertiliser down and were watching grain crops develop fast, they said.
